data.narrative:
Fossa Systems is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Julián Fernández and Vicente González. The target operates within a 14-company private peer set and a 6-ticker public comp universe including RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, and SATL. The company has raised €6.3M to date.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method: stage-progression. Using total capital raised (€6.3M) as a base proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent rounds yields an implied valuation of €12.6M. This anchors the analysis. Public Space & Aerospace comparables trade at a median 27.4x P/S multiple, but cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures. Peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables meeting minimum sample-size thresholds (only two adjacent-stage datapoints identified versus the three-point threshold required).

The analysis supports a valuation range of €11M (low) to €14M (high), with a median estimate of €13M. This range reflects conservative 10% downside and 15% upside variance around the stage-progression central case. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data, limiting deployment of public-comp anchoring, and sparse comparability within the narrow private peer set at this stage. Any subsequent valuation assessment should prioritize obtaining revenue or growth-rate disclosure to enable public-multiple application and strengthen triangulation confidence.
